speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly what happens when you wake up frightened? Do you remember having a nightmare, or do you feel like you're still asleep and can't move?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does she recall any specific details of a dream or nightmare after waking up, or does she have no memory of the event at all? Additionally, do these episodes tend to happen in the first third of the night or later in the sleep cycle?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since she recalls the bad dreams and can be consoled, this points toward nightmares rather than sleep terrors. To rule out other causes, are there any stressors at school or home, and does she snore or have pauses in breathing during sleep?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Met all developmental milestones with no significant medical history. Social history: Attends school regularly, with usual playing habits and interactions with peers. Lives with both parents.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does she experience any daytime symptoms such as excessive sleepiness, headaches, or poor concentration at school? I would like to rule out obstructive sleep apnea, which can present with fragmented sleep and night terrors. REQUEST TEST: Polysomnography

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Not indicated at this stage based on history and normal physical examination.

speaker: Patient
text: No significant findings in other systems. No history of trauma or significant stress identified. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the clear recall of bad dreams and the ability to be consoled, these episodes are consistent with nightmare disorder rather than sleep terrors. DIAGNOSIS READY: Nightmare Disorder
